svg.title: Unit 4 Text A Should the Robots be Taxed?

g.text: Unit 4 Text A Should the Robots be Taxed?
What public phenomenon did the author observe?
what worry ties those examples together?
The fear of blank [e.g. human unemployment]
The author views robots in a positive way
★ How does the author view Robots?
Why does he view it this way?
A historical pattern from stone to blank
Changes in tools reorganize and transform work.
The next generation learns new skills.
What historical case shows this pattern?
From Handloom Weaving to Textile Factory Production
Factories set working hours/strict working hours
One worker handled a broader craft
Tasks became narrower and more specialized
Women and children joined a common production process
Their children and families found work in factories and other firms
★ What are the impacts of automation, and how does the author respond to the concerns it raises?
Factories are closing and workers are being replaced by robots.
Factory workers’ children might become blank.
Spare human capacity can be used for
Higher profits may lead to higher corporate taxes.
Robot production and investment create new jobs.
New jobs create new wages and taxes.
The new jobs and taxes may appear in other regions or countries
Society may not provide new jobs quickly enough.
Workers may not develop new skills in time.
Earlier technological changes were also dramatic.
Horses were replaced by railroads, cars, and trucks.
Passenger ships were replaced by airlines.
Modern information speed makes the effects more visible.
How does the author end the argument?
